extraction.name: Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors
extraction.description: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone. The dataset also includes audio data from an airbome microphone used as a reference. The Vibravox corpus contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer. Annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions are also included in the corpus. We conducted a series of experiments on various speech-related tasks, including speech recognition, speech enhancement, and speaker verification. These experiments were carried out using state-of-the-art models to evaluate and compare their performances on signals captured by the different audio sensors offered by the Vibravox dataset, with the aim of gaining a better grasp of their individual characteristics.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Vibravox dataset was developed through a rigorous data collection process involving 200 participants (188 retained after post-processing). It included designing pre-amplification and conditioning circuits for transducers, coding frontend and back-end software for the recording user interface, adapting sensor housings through 3D modeling and printing, and selecting transducer technologies and recording parameters. The recording process consisted of four consecutive steps for each participant: speech-clean (15 minutes of reading sentences), speechless-noisy (2 minutes 24 seconds of silence in a 3D spatialized ambient noise environment), speechless-clean (54 seconds of silence to record physiological and sensor noises), and speech-noisy (54 seconds of speech in a 3D spatialized ambient noise environment).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Experiments, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A small number of audio clips had various shortcomings, including mispronounced sentences, sensors shifting from their initial positions, occasional sensor malfunctions, or instances where a microphone was inadvertently left unequipped, leading to data inconsistencies.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Audio recordings were collected from 188 participants using five body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) and one airborne microphone as a reference. The text read by participants was sourced from a filtered French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice. Ambient noise samples for noisy conditions were obtained from Audio Set and in-house recordings of concerts and street events, spatialized using a 3D sound spatializer.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A 20 Hz high-pass filter was uniformly applied to each acquisition channel to attenuate low-frequency noise and artifacts. The textual data from French Wikipedia was filtered to exclude most proper names, numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, or syntactic errors. Common text normalization operations, such as lowercasing text and removing punctuation (except apostrophes), were also applied.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Initially, 30,568 sentences were collected from 200 participants. A series of three automatic filters were applied to remove utterances with deficiencies: 1) discarding samples with a Phoneme Error Rate (PER) > 10%, 2) discarding samples where the ratio between speech and silence energy levels (SNR) was not greater than 1.5 dB, and 3) discarding samples where the speech sound level was not greater than the mean silence sound level for that sensor. After filtering, 188 participants and 28,471 sentences were retained. For samples that passed filters, Voice Activity Detection (VAD) timestamps were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides, with trimming by 15 ms if adjusted timestamps exceeded original audio boundaries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Linguistic transcriptions and phonetic transcriptions were included. Phonetic transcriptions were generated using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) with the text phonemizer of the CoML lab. A phase of manual phonetic transcription was necessary for unrecognized words or language switches produced by the phonemizer to preserve the minimal French phonetic alphabet.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Manual phonetic transcription was performed for words where the automated phonemizer produced language switches or failed to recognize words, to ensure adherence to the minimal French phonetic alphabet.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The dataset includes 188 participants (97 female, 91 male). The mean age for females is 25.9 years (median 22, min 19, max 59), and for males is 31.4 years (median 27, min 18, max 82). The overall mean age is 28.55 years (median 25, min 18, max 82). A deliberate effort was made to recruit a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: text phonemizer of the CoML lab [63], whisper-timestamped model (based on Whisper [29])
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains speech samples and physiological sounds. Participant age and gender were collected. All necessary measures were taken to protect privacy, including obtaining informed consent, communicating data collection purpose, and ensuring anonymization and encryption of data in accordance with GDPR.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to drive progress in body-conducted speech analysis and support the development of robust communication systems for real-world applications, particularly in noisy environments. Potential applications include military operations, industrial settings, developing voice commands, monitoring vital signs (e.g., heart rate), access control, and intelligence gathering (speaker identification in intercepted transmissions, battlefield forensics for emotional states and life signals).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Vibravox dataset is not the largest existing dataset of its kind. The post-processing filtering, while ensuring rigorous analysis and fair comparison between microphones, excluded a non-negligible amount of data (6% of participants and 6.8% of pronounced sentences), rather than maximizing overall data volume.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suitable for Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine Tuning of models for speech-related tasks such as speech enhancement, speech recognition (speech-to-phonemes), and speaker verification. It can be used to evaluate and compare the performance of models on signals captured by different audio sensors, gain insights into sensor characteristics, simulate real-world noisy scenarios (using data augmentation with speechless-noisy subset), develop voice commands, and monitor vital signs (using the speechless-clean subset).
